findings.description: W1 THE PHASE_17 W1 PROBE WAS RE-RUN BY ITS ORIGINAL MEASURER ON MERGED MAIN AND THE UNSTAMPED CLASS REPORTS HONESTLY - THE (b)+(c) DECISION CLOSED W1 AT THE TOOL LEVEL, AND THE REJECTION OF (a) IS VINDICATED. Phase_17 W1 (this reviewer measured it) said: the t106 record is a frozen pre-t105 snapshot whose ac4 cross-check is index-state coupled - replayed on merged main it REDS (10 path-membership mismatches + 10 classification drifts, leg set and headline counts agreeing). This review re-ran that exact probe NOW against the shipped tool at HEAD 0eaf723: 'python3 docs/tools/leg_path_pin_audit.py --index docs/state/merge_test_index.json --against-record docs/state/outputs/t106_checker_b64_findings.json' prints the pin set, then 'UNSTAMPED note: record ... carries no index_stamp (no declared git_blob_id) - its observations cannot be classified against this index; a legacy record is REPORTED, not gated on' and exits 0. That is the honest third behavior the contract demanded: NOT a silent RED (which would false-alarm every pre-stamp record against every later index), NOT a false PASS-by-silence (the note names the record and states why classification is impossible), but a computed disclosure. The other three classes were re-measured independently, not taken from the verifier's log: same-blob stamped replay of the companion exits 0 with 22 EXPECTED lines and ZERO DRIFT lines; a mutated copy (leg 230's observation rewritten to a nonexistent card path) exits 1 printing DRIFT lines naming the leg AND the AGAINST-RECORD GATE line; and the W1 scenario itself - the companion record (stamped a4e6509856cf) replayed against the historical index blob 03f01d497914 extracted via 'git show 4dff135d:...' - exits 0 classifying 20 observation differences EXPECTED (stamp mismatch) with 11 in agreement, naming both blobs. An unreadable record path exits 0 with an UNREADABLE-RECORD note (the fifth honest class the verifier bit). The definer decision (b)+(c)-rejecting-(a) is judged CORRECT on the merged bytes: option (a) would have destroyed the property phase_17 W1/W9 credited (the t106 blob is the t106v-verified artifact), and the stamp-alone half of (b) without (c) would leave the classification to human reading-comprehension. Measured corroboration that the rejection was real: the t106 record at HEAD carries NO index_stamp key (json key scan) and its blob is 484d096e9b04 at HEAD - identical to the blob phase_17 review recorded - as is t104's c5ed9bb597ee. RESIDUAL, disclosed not hidden: the t106 CARD's own ac4 fence still REDs when re-run verbatim on merged main (it is a closed card's frozen evidence and cannot be upgraded - which is exactly why the companion+instrument route was chosen); the phase-level instrument is now honest even though that one historical fence is not, and the card's Context states this openly.

W2 THE STAMPED COMPANION RECORD'S replay_contract IS ENFORCEABLE - VERIFIED BY REGENERATION AND COMPARISON, NOT BY READING THE PROSE. This review recomputed the stamp from scratch: a hashlib git-blob id over the CR-normalized index bytes equals the record's index_stamp.git_blob_id (a4e6509856cf2029e0951facf07ac98eeb8d0265), sha256 of the same bytes equals sha256_cr_normalized (5790c1f91f31...), the normalized length equals bytes_cr_normalized (1,304,097), and a fresh run of the shipped auditor on the same index reproduces the record's per_path_status observation-for-observation across all 13 pinned legs with an EMPTY mismatch list - i.e. the record is regenerable semantics-equal from the tool plus the index alone, which is what makes its replay_contract ('replay against a DIFFERENT blob is expected to mismatch; --against-record classifies; no stamp -> UNSTAMPED') an enforceable statement rather than a comment. The contract text names all four operative tokens (index_stamp.git_blob_id, EXPECTED, DRIFT, UNSTAMPED) so a reader cannot follow it into an undefined class. The stamp is a MEASUREMENT provenance chain, not a purity pin: provenance_commit 2f70707 is explicitly labeled provenance-only and no fence quotes it, consistent with the t102 lesson. Recorded as a warning (not a clean finding) for one substantive reason: the companion record is regenerable, so a future index change makes it STALE-BY-STAMP rather than wrong - the stamp mismatch class makes that staleness self-announcing (this review proved it by replaying against the historical blob), but whoever next edits the index owes a regenerated companion, and nothing fences that yet because no future card exists to fence; the stamp design makes the debt visible instead of silent, which was the phase's whole objective.

W3 PLAN.MD NOW MATCHES SHIPPED TRUTH - INDEPENDENTLY CROSS-CHECKED AGAINST t105_repremise_decisions.json AND THE INDEX BY THIS REVIEW, 0-BASED, LEG FOR LEG. This review parsed the shipped decision record and the index's tests array itself (never quoting the card or the fence): read_closed legs = 282 (tests[282]=t76/ac4), 308 (t86/ac3), 309 (t86/ac4); guard_correct_semantics legs = 306 (t86/ac1), 307 (t86/ac2), 310/311/312 (t87/ac1..ac3), 315/316/317 (t88/ac1..ac3) - and plan.md line 2512 now states exactly 'disposition pair read_closed for the 3 live readers (legs 282, 308, 309) vs guard_correct_semantics for the 8 dead-constant legs (legs 306, 307, 310, 311, 312, 315, 316, 317)' with the appended clause that the hygiene-move disposition was REFUSED on every one of the eleven legs - reporting the refusal instead of merely omitting the word, which is the stronger correction. The four rejected strings (byte_hygiene_move, 'REJECTS guard_correct_semantics', GREEN-but-silently-degraded, 'guards skip the probe') measure ZERO whole-file occurrences in plan.md; the corrected mechanism sentence 'Liveness was MEASURED, not assumed' survives (exactly 1); the phase_17 section carries each disposition word exactly once (the corrected line); and the phase_18 section's provenance lines restate the split correctly (which is why WAL 1252's 'guard_correct_semantics present x2 in plan.md' is consistent, not drift). The phase_18 section also carries the style rule (rejected strings DESCRIBED, never quoted) that keeps the global-absence fence durable. Verdict on the definer custody judgment embedded in the card: keeping the historical phase_17 survey/review handoffs frozen (the same strings still exist there - this review counted 1 each in both) while correcting only the forward-looking plan document is the right scope, for the same custody reason t107 rejected regenerating the t106 record, and both cards state the reason in writing.

W4 THE WAL 1248 W3 OVERSTATEMENT CORRECTION IS JUDGED: PROCESS WORKED EXACTLY AS AN APPEND-ONLY LEDGER SHOULD - MEASURED, RECORDED, NOT SILENTLY FIXED. WAL 1248 W3 (orchestrator-authored) said plan.md carried the 'REJECTS guard_correct_semantics for all eleven' claim; the definer measured at groom time that the string occurs ZERO times in plan.md and disclosed the overstatement, and WAL 1250 records the orchestrator's acceptance ('my WAL 1248 W3 wording overstated plan.md content'). This review verified the measurement against the base blob: plan.md at 2f70707 holds byte_hygiene_move x1, GREEN-but-silently-degraded x1, 'guards skip the probe' x1, 'test -f' x1 - and REJECTS-guard_correct_semantics x0; the two phase_17 handoffs hold it x1 each (the string lived only in definer handoff prose, never in the plan). Judgment: (1) the correction was MEASURED before it was asserted - and the t108 ac1 fence then planted each needle through its own detect() to prove the absence was a measured absence rather than a vacuous pass, which is the correct response to having just been burned by an overstated absence; (2) the wrong entry was NOT rewritten - WAL 1248 stands as history and WAL 1250 carries the correction, which is the only shape compatible with the WAL being evidence; (3) the direction of the error matters: the orchestrator OVERSTATED a defect and the correction made the defect smaller, so the correction was independently checkable by anyone with grep. The class is not eliminated - a WAL entry remains prose until fenced - but the handling is the exemplar: measure, disclose in the next entry, accept, and build the plant-and-prove fence.

W5 THE merge_sha AMEND-REGRESS PROCESS DEFECT IS JUDGED: SELF-DISCLOSED, CORRECTED WITHOUT REWRITING HISTORY, AND THE NEW CONVENTION IS THE RIGHT PERMANENT FIX. WAL 1252 discloses that the merge-history backfill script amended the merge commit to record its own merge_sha and therefore recorded the PRE-amend sha (6f64fc0 for t107, b6f03b8 for t108) - the classic self-reference regress: amending to record a sha changes the sha, so the recorded value can never be true inside its own commit. This review verified the correction on the merged tree: merge_history entries now carry merge_sha fae71578ae1b6635337572e602522866d38bab70 and 048039c4575085e7a245078243db2c565737c33a, both of which resolve as real commits (git rev-parse read-back), both notes state 'merge_sha recorded in follow-up commit', t107's note discloses the pre-amend sha, and the corrections ride ordinary follow-up commits a190fa0 and 281b6de rather than amends. Judgment: the follow-up-commit convention is correct and should stand as policy - a commit's identity is only statable from OUTSIDE itself, so the only honest record is a later one; the amend attempt was a script defect, not a custody breach (it touched only merge_history bookkeeping the orchestrator owns, was caught in the same window, and the false shas were disclosed rather than quietly replaced). Residual: merge_history is now append-mostly by convention, not by fence, and the pre-amend shas 6f64fc0/b6f03b8 remain dangling disclosed references (harmless - they are disclosed as pre-amend, not asserted as merges).

W6 DEVIATION AUDIT: NO NEW DEVIATIONS THIS PHASE - THE LABEL-CUSTODY PRECEDENT (WAL 1244) WAS HONORED BY BOTH VERIFIERS, VERIFIED FROM THEIR OWN HANDOFFS. This review read the platform/label sections of both verifier handoffs rather than trusting the WAL summary: t107v records 'Verifier did NOT self-apply any platform label and made NO platform write (no comment post, no label add/remove). Orchestrator owns the built->verified transition and the verdict comment on issue #113', and t108v records the same with zero platform.ts calls (t106v's phase_17 self-application, the deviation WAL 1244 absorbed, did not recur). The card-path naming deviation t108v disclosed (task text said 't108_verifier_verify.json', the skill/precedent name t108_verifier_verify_issue.json shipped) is skill-over-task-text and correctly resolved. The handoff-placement disclosure (the verifier handoff commit REDs ac4/ac6 at the post-verification tip by construction, probed in a throwaway clone, t106 precedent) is the known phase_16/17 artifact, not a product defect. Both builders' environment repairs (t108b's .git-pointer repair to the relative convention; the WAL 1251 WSL-CWD lesson) are disclosed env facts with zero tracked bytes. Nothing in the phase required an operator decision that was not asked.

W7 SWEEP INTERPRETATION STANDS UP UNDER INDEPENDENT RE-DERIVATION. Post-merge 318-leg sweep on final main d8120e0: GREEN 282 / RED 36 vs the phase_17 baseline 281/37 (WAL 1253). The recovered leg, 1-based 190 = 0-based 189, is t47's uv/alembic leg - this review read tests[189] in the index directly and confirms it carries NO ac key and NO card-path pin (its command is a uv/PATH probe), matching the known transient docker/uv flake classification carried across phase_16/17 (rc=0 standalone twice), so the GREEN return is the flake clearing, not a masked repair. NEW RED: EMPTY SET - zero regressions, which for this phase is corroborated structurally as well as empirically: t107 changed only a tool under docs/tools and a new record (the checker's ungiven output is byte-identical to base per its own ac5, and the companion record is data, not code - it adds no pins, proven by the 13-pin set naming only t62/t76/t78/t86 paths), and t108 changed only plan.md prose, which no sweep leg reads. Expected-still-RED confirmed leg-for-leg: 1-based 310 = 0-based 309 (t86/ac4, the disclosed pinned-BASE 67c9db975d75 residue - orchestrator index-defect custody, untouched by design since the phase carried ZERO index bytes) and 1-based 231 = 0-based 230 (t62/ac6, the frozen plaintext analogue). The archival triple-proof (raw index carries no t107/t108 literals; matrix generator re-run byte-equal rows=749 gap=0 unpointed=0; t78 exemption intact) is consistent with the checker run this review executed at HEAD: pinned_legs=13, broken_pins=0, dirty_b64_legs=0.

W8 COVERAGE: BOTH OPERATOR-AUTHORIZED ITEMS (WAL 1249 items 1+2) ARE COVERED, THE THIRD IS AN EXPLICIT BACKLOG DEFERRAL NOT A GAP, AND NEITHER CARD MOVES A REQUIREMENT. Against docs/requirements.md and plan.md's phase_18 section: t107 covers the W1 remedy (stamp + instrument + companion record, the shape WAL 1249 demanded - 'must make ac4-replay index-state EXPLICIT and must not silently rewrite history semantics' - satisfied literally: the replay is explicit via the stamp and the t106 record is untouched), t108 covers the W3 docs-drift cleanup (plan.md vocabulary + rejected-mechanism prose vs shipped records, docs-only surface). Item 3 (193/318 legs lacking the ac key) was explained to the operator and LEFT IN STANDING BACKLOG by explicit instruction (WAL 1249) - recorded here so a future coverage check does not report the deferral as this milestone's gap. Neither card introduces or deletes a REQ-ID (both state NO NEW REQ-ID; t107 cites only the t104/t106 checker/hygiene anchor families, t108 claims no anchors - documentation truth only), docs/requirements.md and all six criteria docs are byte-frozen by both cards' fences (t108 ac5 proves it against the run-time base), and the archival matrix re-run was byte-equal (rows=749 gap=0 unpointed=0). No coverage_gap error: the milestone satisfies WAL 1249 as written.

W9 GRANULARITY: t107 SITS AT THE AC CEILING AND OVER THE NOMINAL LINE CEILING (warn_only), t108 IS TRIVIAL, AND THE SURVEY'S granularity_check DISAGREES WITH THE CONFIG A THIRD TIME. docs/config.yaml limits.issue_granularity: max_acs=6, max_files=4, max_diff_lines=300, warn_only=true. Measured: t107 = 6 ACs (at ceiling), 2 product files (merge numstat: leg_path_pin_audit.py 159/1 + t107_record_stamp_findings.json 327/0 = 487 diff lines, over the nominal 300 - the same machine-generated-record overage class as phase_17 W6's 470), t108 = 6 ACs, 1 file, 3/3 = 6 lines (the smallest product delta of the run). Neither card was splittable: the operator directed exactly two cards (WAL 1249), and each deliverable set is indivisible (one tool upgrade + its stamped record; one prose correction). The ~900-line card bodies are evidence fences, not scope. The recurring defect is the survey handoff's granularity_check, which this phase reported max_files_per_issue=2 / within_limits=true where the config says 4 - the THIRD consecutive phase (phase_16 W5, phase_17 W6, now phase_18) in which survey restates granularity numbers that do not match docs/config.yaml instead of reading it; the within_limits conclusion happens to be right for the wrong stated reason. Actionable: the survey step should load limits.issue_granularity from config rather than re-deriving it by eye.

W10 STEP 3 CLEAN: NO CYCLE, NO DANGLING EDGE, NO ORPHAN DEFECT - AND THE ROOT-CARD COUNT IS RECORDED SO A FUTURE CHECK DOES NOT MISTAKE ROOTS FOR ORPHANS. Against docs/state/dag.json: 109 nodes, 144 edges, zero edges referencing a non-existent node, cycles=[] (depth-first coloring over the full graph), and t107/t108 each carry in-degree 0 and out-degree 0 - matching both cards' declared depends: [] and both plan lines, and matching the execution shape (worktrees t107b/t108b both cut from 2f70707, builders dispatched together, merges fae7157 then 048039c serialized per WAL 1140). Twelve nodes now carry no edge (t72, t73, t74, t96, t97, t101, t103, t104, t105, t106, t107, t108); all twelve are deliberate root cards from later phases, and this is the phase_17 W8 count plus the two new roots - recorded, not a defect. The parallel-safety claim was structural, not asserted: the two cards share no path (checker+companion record vs plan.md), each freezes the other's surface by bytes against a run-time-derived base, and the merges landed in either-order-safe shape (t108's ac4 froze t107's absent-at-base-and-tree state correctly; t107's ac6 hard-froze plan.md, which t108 had not yet touched at its base).

W11 STEP 4 CLEAN: NO DUPLICATED AND NO CONTRADICTORY AC BETWEEN THE CARDS - AND THE ONLY IN-CARD VERIFICATION DRIFT REVIEW FOUND IS DOCUMENTARY, INSIDE t108's ac2 HEADING/COMMENT, NOT IN THE ENFORCED BODY. Both cards' closeout fences restate the same phase_15 rule (run-time base derivation, WAL excluded, ac_hash recomputed) with disjoint bodies and disjoint owned surfaces - the established non-duplicate pattern. The one nit this review measured: t108's ac2 heading and the fence's own COMMENT claim a whole-file token count ('guard_correct_semantics exactly 8, read_closed exactly 3 - the only place either word appears in plan.md'), but the shipped fence CODE checks something different and stricter-in-scope: a run-time parse of the decision record for the exact 3/8 split, the contracted one-line pair inside the phase_17 section, and exactly-one-occurrence-per-word INSIDE THAT SECTION - because the phase_18 section legitimately names the split as provenance (whole-file counts are 2 and 2, not 8 and 3). The comment's claim is therefore stale prose against its own body, and the ac2 heading's 'token counts equal a fresh count' wording does not describe what the code enforces; the CODE is the contract (the ac_hash is defined over the fenced bodies, all four handoffs agree on 1db2c5b7ff4f, and the verifier ran the shipped body verbatim), so nothing was verified less than needed - but a card whose heading overstates its fence is the same species of drift this phase exists to retire, now observed inside a card rather than the plan, and the stray '### ac2 is defined below' line between t108's ac2 heading and its fence is a cosmetic sibling of the same slip (harmless to the fence regex - gate1, the six-block check and the four-way ac_hash all passed). Recorded as a warning against the closed card: no re-groom is warranted because the enforced surface is correct and merged; the actionable residue is that heading/comment text should be generated from, or checked against, the fence body it describes.

W12 MILESTONE BOOKKEEPING AND SCOPE OF THIS REVIEW: Step 6 APPLIED TO ITSELF (the phase_15 W6 / phase_16 W8 / phase_17 W11 precedent, disclosed rather than silently varied), and NOTHING ELSE WAS TOUCHED. docs/state/milestones/phase_18_record_stamp_plan_drift.json now carries review_plan_status=passed, review_plan_completed_at=2026-10-22T06:20:00Z, review_plan_verdict=PASS_WITH_WARNINGS and review_plan_attempts 0 -> 1. Both cards are already closed [verified] (#113/#114, WAL 1253) and archived, so this is a post-milestone plan-split review whose corroborating proof is the milestone's own closeout evidence (WAL 1252's verdict window and WAL 1253's 282/36 sweep). Per this task's order the definer committed these two files as a docs-only commit and PUSHED (one git op per cmd.exe call with read-back); no product file, no card, no DAG, no index byte, no merge_history entry and no platform call was made by this review. Every probe this review ran was read-only or ran on throwaway copies in /tmp: the four --against-record classes, the stamp recomputation, the record regeneration comparison, the plan-vs-record leg derivation, and the DAG cycle scan - the tracked tree was byte-clean before and after (the only porcelain entry is the pre-existing untracked docs/state/history/, not this review's).
